definition: commercial activity or a person's work or trade.
example: Her family runs a small business in the suburb.
originNote: from busy, meaning occupied.
spellingTip: Say BIZ-nis, but remember the middle is -iness reduced.

definition: more than usually or particularly.
example: I enjoyed the film, especially the ending.
originNote: from special, meaning particular.
spellingTip: It is e-special-ly, not expecially.

definition: easy to see or recognise.
example: There was a noticeable change in his attitude.
originNote: from notice, meaning observe.
spellingTip: Keep the e before -able: notice + able.

definition: feeling ashamed or awkward.
example: I felt embarrassed after calling the teacher by the wrong name.
originNote: from a word meaning hindered or obstructed.
spellingTip: Think em + barr + assed: double r and double s.

definition: in a personal or secret way.
example: She spoke privately with the coach after training.
originNote: from private, meaning personal.
spellingTip: Drop the final e before adding -ly.

definition: to cease to be seen or present.
example: My notes always disappear when I need them most.
originNote: from appear with negative prefix dis-.
spellingTip: It has double p in appear after dis-.

definition: a person or thing liked more than others.
example: That song is still my favourite from the album.
originNote: from favour, meaning approval.
spellingTip: In Australian spelling, keep the ou in favour.

definition: a strong desire to know or learn something.
example: Her curiosity led her to ask thoughtful questions.
originNote: from curious, meaning eager to know.
spellingTip: The middle is -ios-, not -ous-.

definition: in a sincere or real way.
example: He was genuinely pleased by the compliment.
originNote: from genuine, meaning natural or true.
spellingTip: Remember genuine keeps the u before ine.

definition: able to be used, obtained, or reached.
example: Tickets are still available online.
originNote: from avail, meaning help or benefit.
spellingTip: Hear avail inside available before -able.

definition: playfully causing trouble or annoyance.
example: The puppy gave us a mischievous look before stealing the sock.
originNote: from mischief, meaning trouble or harm.
spellingTip: It ends in -ous, not -ious, and has three syllables.

definition: useful or suitable for one's needs.
example: The shop is in a convenient location near the station.
originNote: from convene, meaning come together.
spellingTip: The ending is -ient, not -ant.

definition: to make something seem larger or more important than it is.
example: Try not to exaggerate the problem when you explain it.
originNote: from roots meaning heap up.
spellingTip: It has double g after exa-.

definition: a class or group of similar things.
example: Please put each book into the correct category.
originNote: from a term meaning class or predicate.
spellingTip: Watch the middle: cat-e-gory, not catagory.

definition: from time to time but not regularly.
example: We occasionally go for a walk after dinner.
originNote: from occasion, meaning opportunity or event.
spellingTip: Double c, then sion, then ally.

definition: to recognise the value of something.
example: I really appreciate your help with the project.
originNote: from a root meaning value.
spellingTip: It has double p and ci before ate.

definition: a person living near another person.
example: Our neighbour brought over some fresh lemons.
originNote: from words meaning near dweller.
spellingTip: Australian spelling uses ou in neighbour.

definition: to identify someone or something from previous knowledge.
example: I could hardly recognise him with the new haircut.
originNote: from roots meaning know again.
spellingTip: Use -ise in Australian spelling, not -ize.

definition: training that develops self-control or orderly behaviour.
example: Learning an instrument takes patience and discipline.
originNote: from a word meaning instruction or teaching.
spellingTip: The middle is sci, not si or ci alone.

definition: the necessary items for a purpose or activity.
example: Check the camping equipment before we leave.
originNote: from equip, meaning prepare.
spellingTip: It is equip + ment, so keep the quip.

definition: not connected with the subject being discussed.
example: Several comments were interesting but irrelevant to the debate.
originNote: from roots meaning not lift toward.
spellingTip: Double r after ir-, and the ending is -ant.

definition: a plan showing times for events or tasks.
example: My schedule is full during exam week.
originNote: from a word meaning slip of paper.
spellingTip: Remember sch at the start, not sk.
